executive_assessment.text: Named southern canal pilots and drought/livestock examples distinguish local vulnerabilities and capacities, with older maps and proposed 2021–25 works kept dated.

Chu–Talas evidence identifies allocation/data/infrastructure mediators, and the historical Aspara account describes dialogue/accounting as prevention capacities; neither establishes an isolated climate effect or a general peace-impact estimate.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-05 reports: Water metering in Maktaaral District, Turkestan, cut losses 35-40% on monitored canals in 2019-20.
Source dated 2024-05 reports: A 2021-25 plan targeted 119 canals in four southern regions holding over 85% of irrigated land.
Source dated 2025 reports: The report says 2021 heat reached 46.5°C in Kyzylorda, Mangystau and Turkestan, drying soil and pasture feed.
Source dated 2025 reports: GIZ reports cited findings of Mangystau livestock losses and full runoff use in Shu-Talas and Nura-Sarysu basins.
Source dated 2018-04 reports: World Bank mapped Kyzylorda, Zhambyl, Almaty, East Kazakhstan and Kostanay as climate-susceptible; most farming was in at-risk areas.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 11 of 12 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

No inspected source establishes climate stress as the cause of organized armed violence in Kazakhstan; evidence is of conditional cross-border water tensions, governance mediators and conflict-prevention capacity.
The 2024 flood passage names northern and western Kazakhstan but not affected oblasts, limiting subnational flood mapping.
GIZ omitted hydrological drought and general water depletion projections because data were insufficient; some local impacts rely on secondary citations.
UNDP reports project objectives and dates, not evaluated service-level or resilience outcomes.
The 2024 World Bank Poverty and Equity Assessment full PDF could not be read because it exceeded the web fetch limit; no indexed text was used.
Historical subnational administrative names are retained with source vintage; no current-region or incident map is inferred from older vulnerability maps.
Climate is described as an aggravating factor in qualitative river-basin evidence, not a sufficient cause of cross-border violence; no verified reverse insecurity blockage to adaptation is assembled.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
